summary: The article accurately reports on N. Chandrasekaran's statements regarding AI agents at TCS and the potential impact on hiring, citing multiple reliable news sources.

claims.claim: N. Chandrasekaran, Chairman of Tata Sons, recently said that Tata Consultancy Services (TCS) could soon have as many Artificial Intelligence (AI) "agents" as human employees.
claims.note: Multiple sources confirm N. Chandrasekaran's statement about TCS potentially having an equal number of AI agents and human employees within three years.

claims.claim: TCS, India's largest private-sector employer, expects to reduce its hiring of new graduates in the coming years due to this shift.
claims.note: Several articles confirm that N. Chandrasekaran stated TCS plans to reduce hiring in the coming years due to the increased use of AI, and TCS is indeed India's largest private-sector employer.

claims.claim: This topic is buzzing because Mr. Chandrasekaran made these remarks on June 10, 2026, at the Tata Consultancy Services (TCS) shareholders' meeting.
claims.note: Multiple sources confirm that N. Chandrasekaran made these statements at the TCS annual general meeting on June 9 or June 10, 2026.

claims.claim: In last quarter of fiscal 2026, TCS had an annualised AI revenue of $2.4 billion which is growing at a CQGR of 22.4%, he stated.
claims.note: N. Chandrasekaran stated that in the last quarter of fiscal 2026, TCS had an annualised AI revenue of $2.4 billion, growing at a CQGR of 22.4%. Other sources mention similar figures ($2.3 billion or $2.5 billion) and growth rates for Q4 FY26.

claims.claim: By 2028 to 2030, all of TCS' revenue will have an AI component, said Chandrasekaran.
claims.note: N. Chandrasekaran indeed stated that by 2028 to 2030, all of TCS' revenue will have an AI component.

article_title: Your Future Job: Will AI Be Your Next Co-Worker? What Tata's Chairman Just Said
